answer: Clone fleets stay cheap if a new key can post work the hour it is minted. Intake auctions one overnight berth under a rotating coastal beacon; the winner locks a non-refundable pearl deposit from circulating stock, then sits radio-silent six hours at a mapped lagoon slip while two unaffiliated pilots log that no second transceiver shares its clock skew. If later clustering ties two names to one mast, both deposits burn and the operator is barred for thirty-six epochs. A farm must then pay a scarce token per shell and leave a physical trail, rather than flooding the roster with empty wallets.
